We focus on instances that satisfy strengthened assumption of Local Lemma of the form 2 1 − α ​ k ​ ( Δ + 1 ) ​ e < 1 , 2^{1-\alpha k}(\Delta+1)\mathrm{e}<1, where Δ \Delta is the bound on the maximum edge degree of the hypergraph.

arxiv-2308-04640.title: Demonstration of Orbit Determination for LEO Objects using the Murchison Widefield Array DOI: 10.1017/pas.2026.xxx
arxiv-2308-04640.creator: Prabu, S. 1,4, Hancock, P. 2, Zhang, X. 3,5, and Tingay, S.J. 1
arxiv-2308-04640.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Prabu, S. 1,4, Hancock, P. 2, Zhang, X. 3,5, and Tingay, S.J. 1. The rapidly increasing number of satellites in Earth’s orbit motivates the development of Space Domain Awareness (SDA) capabilities using wide field-of-view sensor systems that can perform simultaneous detections. This work demonstrates preliminary orbit determination capability for Low Earth Orbit objects using the 36 ∘ × 36 ∘ 36^{\circ}\times 36^{\circ} field-of-view of the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) at commercial Frequency Modulated (FM) frequencies (transmitters in 88 − 108 88-108 MHz range).

arxiv-2310-10273.title: Tensor glueball decay into nucleon-antinucleon
arxiv-2310-10273.creator: A. Vereijken \from ins:x
arxiv-2310-10273.description: Abstract In the context of a chiral hadronic model, we compute the decay ratio of a tensor glueball decaying into a nucleon and antinucleon compared to the decay into 2 pions. Tensor meson dominance is assumed to also hold for the tensor glueball in order to relate the coupling constants of the different decay channels.

arxiv-2311-03269.title: Metachronal coordination at the mesoscale
arxiv-2311-03269.creator: Sebastian Ziegler 1,† , Megan Delens 2,† , Ylona Collard 2 , Maxime Hubert 1,3 , Nicolas Vandewalle 2,∗ , and Ana-Sunčana Smith 1,3,
arxiv-2311-03269.description: Abstract In nature, metachronal coordination is an efficient strategy for fluid pumping and self-propulsion. Yet, mimetic systems for this type of organization are scarce. Recently, metachronal motion was observed in a bead-based magnetocapillary mesoswimmer, but the mechanism of such device’s behavior remained unclear.

arxiv-2404-11775.creator: Evan Habbershaw, Cory Hauck, Jingwei Hu, Jeffrey R. Haack
arxiv-2404-11775.description: Abstract A multi-species Fokker-Planck model for simulating particle collisions in a plasma is presented. The model includes various parameters that must be tuned. Under reasonable assumptions on these parameters, the model satisfies appropriate conservation laws, dissipates an entropy, and satisfies an ℋ \mathcal{H} -Theorem.

arxiv-2405-08295.title: SpeechVerse: A Large-scale Generalizable Audio Language Model
arxiv-2405-08295.creator: Nilaksh Das *, Saket Dingliwal, Srikanth Ronanki, Rohit Paturi, Zhaocheng Huang, Prashant Mathur, Jie Yuan, Dhanush Bekal, Xing Niu, Sai Muralidhar Jayanthi, Xilai Li, Karel Mundnich, Monica Sunkara, Sravan Bodapati, Sundararajan Srinivasan, Daniel Garcia-Romero, Kyu J. Han, Katrin Kirchhoff
arxiv-2405-08295.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown incredible proficiency in performing tasks that require semantic understanding of natural language instructions. Recently, many works have further expanded this capability to perceive multimodal audio and text inputs, but their capabilities are often limited to specific fine-tuned tasks such as automatic speech recognition and translation.

arxiv-2406-10778.title: Heterogeneous Entity Representation for Medicinal Synergy Prediction
arxiv-2406-10778.creator: Jiawei Wu †, Jun Wen †, Mingyuan Yan †, Anqi Dong, Shuai Gao, Ren Wang, Can Chen
arxiv-2406-10778.description: Abstract Motivation: Forecasting the synergistic effects of drug combinations facilitates drug discovery and development, especially regarding cancer therapeutics. While numerous computational methods have emerged, most of them fall short in fully modeling the relationships among clinical entities including drugs, cell lines, and diseases, which hampers their ability to generalize to drug combinations involving unseen drugs.

arxiv-2412-11662.title: Unitary n n -correlations with restricted support in random matrix theory
arxiv-2412-11662.creator: Patrik Demjan and N. C. Snaith
arxiv-2412-11662.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Patrik Demjan and N. C. Snaith. We consider the n n -correlation of eigenvalues of random unitary matrices in the alternative form that is not the tidy determinant common in random matrix theory, but rather the expression derived from averages of ratios of characteristic polynomials in a method that can be mimicked in number theoretical calculations of the correlations of zeros of L L -functions.

arxiv-2509-11818.title: SCDTour: Embedding Axis Ordering and Merging for Interpretable Semantic Change Detection
arxiv-2509-11818.creator: Taichi Aida, Danushka Bollegala
arxiv-2509-11818.description: Abstract In SCD ( SCD ), it is a common problem to obtain embeddings that are both interpretable and high-performing. However, improving interpretability often leads to a loss in the SCD performance, and vice versa. To address this problem, we propose SCD Tour, a method that orders and merges interpretable axes to alleviate the performance degradation of SCD .

pmc-10521393.description: BackgroundVitamin D Deficiency is recognized as a pandemic, which is associated with high mortality. An inadequate level of vitamin D is associated with autoimmune diseases, hypertension, and cancer. The study was aimed to assess the pharmacological effects of chronic vitamin D3 supplementation on the manipulation diet regiment of deprived cholecalciferol (vitamin D3 deficient diet, VDD) rats.

pmc-10526648.creator: Luísa Fialho, Augusto Costa-Barbosa, Paula Sampaio, Sandra Carvalho
pmc-10526648.description: The deposition of zinc–zinc oxide nanoparticles (Zn–ZnO NPs) onto porous Ta2O5 surfaces enriched with calcium phosphate by DC magnetron sputtering was investigated to improve the surface antimicrobial activity without triggering an inflammatory response. Different sizes and amounts of Zn NPs obtained by two optimized different depositions and an additional thin carbon (C) layer deposited over the NPs were explored.

pmc-12427365.title: Liposomal Doxorubicin, but Not Platinum-Taxane, Supports MHC-II Expression and Immune Maturation in the Ovarian Tumor Microenvironment
pmc-12427365.creator: Hyojae Lee, Xiao-Lei Chen, Duygu Ozmadenci, Elise Tahon, Terrance J Haanan, Breana Hill, Safir Ullah Khan, Antonia Boyer, David D Schlaepfer, Dwayne Stupack, Edward J Pavlik
pmc-12427365.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryChemotherapy is now appreciated for its ability to promote immunogenic cell death, yet many studies have not replicated effective preclinical dosing that provides effective tumor control. We used efficacious doses for tumor control and six cycles of a first-line therapy (platinum and taxane, P/T) or a second-line therapy (pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, PLD) and evaluated their impact on the immune and tumor compartments of an aggressive murine model of ovarian carcinoma.

pmc-12734795.description: Carbon membranes have emerged as a promising class of inorganic membranes for desalination due to their tunable pore structures, superior chemical and thermal stability, and molecular-sieving properties. pmc-13101558.title: Characterization of a novel inherited splice-site variant in MAPK8IP3 expands the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders
pmc-13101558.creator: Sheng Yi, Qi Yang, Xiong Song, Limei Huang, Shang Yi, Zailong Qin, Jingsi Luo
pmc-13101558.description: BackgroundThe MAPK8IP3 gene encodes JIP3, a kinesin-1 adapter protein crucial for axonal transport and JNK signaling pathway regulation. This gene exhibits extreme intolerance to loss-of-function variants. Heterozygous pathogenic MAPK8IP3 variants are linked to a neurodevelopmental disorder with or without variable brain abnormalities (NEDBA). This study characterizes a novel inherited canonical splice-site variant identified in a three-generation family.

pmc-13326407.title: A macrogenetic analysis of isolation mechanisms shaping genetic divergence in mammals
pmc-13326407.creator: Daniel A Hancock, Patrick Meirmans
pmc-13326407.description: Understanding the processes that shape spatial genetic differentiation is essential for understanding how populations adapt to environmental change. By evaluating the influence of these processes, we can gain insights into evolutionary dynamics and the potential for species to respond to shifting landscapes.
